verdict: DEFER. Full text is open access but unreachable from this network; the abstract alone does not engage land value, rent, land value tax, betterment or Georgist ideas, so an abstract-level ENRICH would be thin and mostly a bare citation. Re-try the full text (a fetch from a different network, or a human download of the OA PDF to the scratch folder) before any page work. If full text is later obtained and confirms substantive treatment of land value capture or the 'land as a shared trust' foundation, the candidate home is ENRICH concepts/land-as-commons.md (a sentence in the commons-trust/Ostrom comparison paragraph, after the sentence ending 'address different questions: Ostrom asks how commons are governed; George asks who is entitled to the rent they generate.') plus a one-line See Also bullet in research/rahmawati-indonesia-land-banking-housing.md under 'Relation to the Georgist Case' and, only if the Haven-Stad illustration is substantive on land value, one sentence in places/netherlands.md. Not NEW: a conceptual framework with no empirical findings does not merit its own research page on the abstract. Not REJECT: the paper is peer-reviewed, by a recognised Dutch land-policy scholar, and its reference list includes value-capture items.
claim_grade: D-claim as to any Georgist or rent content (nothing in the accessible material supports it); the abstract-level descriptive facts (what the paper argues; that its propositions are 'conjectures rather than validated findings') are A-claim on the abstract text. Source tier under EDITORIAL 4c: Tier 1 proposed (see uncertainties) for the author's own scholarly framework, but the paper is a conceptual proposal with no tested findings, so it cannot be cited as evidence that any Georgist claim is right.

content_summary.point: Core thesis: land governance fails because land use, land rights and land value are treated as parallel administrative domains instead of mutually constitutive components of one recursive structure; outcomes are a function of alignment among them.
content_summary.quote: treatment of land use, land rights, and land value as parallel administrative domains rather than as mutually constitutive components of one recursive governance structure

content_summary.point: Method and status: targeted review of existing frameworks; four foundations (three analytical: institutional economics/property rights, game theory, adaptive governance; one normative: political philosophy and critical land studies); four propositions explicitly labelled conjectures.
content_summary.quote: The propositions are conjectures rather than validated findings

content_summary.point: Normative foundation: land as a shared trust 'defining what alignment is for'. The abstract gives no detail on whether this is tied to land rent, land value capture or George; that cannot be asserted from the abstract.
content_summary.quote: establishes land as a shared trust defining what alignment is for
content_summary.grep: shared trust defining what alignment is for

content_summary.point: Three claims: configurations are strategically produced and defended by actors; alignment is the condition for planning interventions to achieve intended outcomes; governance is an ongoing search constrained by path dependence, capture and culturally institutionalised models.
content_summary.quote: constrained by path dependence, capture, and culturally institutionalised models of governance

content_summary.point: Illustrations: Sayung (Indonesia) and Haven-Stad (Amsterdam); the abstract says only that the framework identifies mechanisms of misalignment existing frameworks struggle to explain; no empirical findings or figures. 'Capture' in the abstract is institutional/regulatory capture, not rent capture.
content_summary.quote: Two illustrations, Sayung in Indonesia and Haven-Stad in Amsterdam

content_summary.point: Reference list (49 items) contains value-capture-adjacent works: Alterman 2012 'Land use regulations and property values: the windfalls capture idea revisited'; Samsura 2012 'Negotiating land and property development: A game theoretical approach to value capturing'; Van der Krabben 2013 'Public land development as a strategic tool for redevelopment: Reflections on the Dutch experience'; plus Rawls 1971, Ostrom 2009, North 1990. No entry for Henry George, Progress and Poverty, land value tax, betterment or economic rent (grep for 'george' in the references file returns 0). Whether the body text discusses these is unknown.
content_summary.quote: Land use regulations and property values: the “windfalls capture” idea revisited

content_summary.point: Reference to the author's own value-capture game-theory work

uncertainties: Full text not reached: everything about the body (what 'shared trust' means, any treatment of land value, rent, betterment, LVT or George, the Sayung and Haven-Stad details, quotable passages with page locators) is unknown. The reference list suggests value capturing is a sub-theme (Alterman, Samsura 2012), but a reference list is not a treatment.

Proposed 4c tier for Samsura: Tier 1 (recognised academic), on these grounds: Radboud University Nijmegen (Department of Geography, Spatial Planning and Environment, per OpenAlex affiliation); peer-reviewed venue (Land Use Policy, an established Elsevier journal, ranked ABDC-A per OpenAlex); a prior body of work on land development and value capturing (Samsura 2010, 2012, listed in the paper's own references; co-author with Erwin van der Krabben on the wiki's existing Rahmawati page). Neither Samsura nor van der Krabben is in sources/audit/people-tiers.json, so this is a rubric judgement, not a listed ruling. Caveat: a Tier 1 standing does not make a self-described conjectural framework evidence; cite it as 'a proposed conceptual framework', never as support for Georgist claims.

Licence strings conflict (Crossref/Elsevier: CC BY 4.0; Unpaywall/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar: cc-by-nc-nd). Matters only if the text is later quoted at length; quotes of <=50 words are fine either way.
Publication metadata: online 2026-09-22 (Crossref created), cover date January 2027, volume 172, article number 108346; cited_by 0, so no secondary commentary exists yet.

The queue item's description of the paper (Sayung, Haven-Stad, four propositions, shared trust) is confirmed by the abstract; its suggestion that the paper engages 'rent-seeking' and 'land value' as a Georgist-adjacent domain is not confirmed (the abstract says capture, not rent capture).
